clue.text: Initially under training in, for example, Texas law

indicators.note: in signals that the pair of initials goes inside the other piece

parts.note: Texas is an example of a US state

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A Texas statute laying down that trainees should be put through their paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' gives UT from under and training; 'in' places UT inside STATE, after its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a written law passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Sneak away and get partly undressed

explanation.surface: Someone leaving quietly while shedding a layer of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To slip off is both to leave unnoticed and to remove a garment, leaving one partly unclothed.

clue.text: First male worker was unyielding

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is the first man
a worker is a classic crossword ant, a worker insect

explanation.surface: The first man, as a labourer, refused to give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is only a link between wordplay and the adjective at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant describes someone firm and refusing to be persuaded, a close synonym.

clue.text: Christian attending first university

indicators.note: first says the university piece comes before the other piece

parts.note: attending means being at, giving at

explanation.surface: A Christian student going up to university for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A Uniat is a member of an Eastern church in union with Rome, so a kind of Christian.

clue.text: Trace exit in order to set free

indicators.note: putting letters in order suggests rearranging them into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Following the way out in order to escape.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free someone or something from a difficulty or entanglement.

clue.text: Will's night at the end of Christmas

definitions.text: Will's night at the end of Christmas

parts.words: Will's night at the end of Christmas
parts.note: Will is William Shakespeare, whose comedy is named after the last night of the twelve days of Christmas, the eve of Epiphany

explanation.surface: A man named Will celebrating the final night of the Christmas season.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelfth night after Christmas closes the festive season and titles Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Object to poor government

annotationWithheld.why: Object to poor government (5): THING gives 'Object' and the Norse assembly sense, but 'poor' has no job in any parse

clue.text: By a stream flowing outwards

annotationWithheld.why: By a stream flowing outwards (9): CURRENT is 'stream' but no reading makes 'By a' give EX

clue.text: Retired at full speed ahead!

parts.note: at top speed, and also lying exhausted, as one who has turned in for the night after racing

explanation.surface: Someone going to bed in a hurry, as if racing full speed ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out is an idiom for going as fast as possible, and also for lying spread out asleep.

clue.text: Well informed about a spasm acting on the liver

parts.note: hep is dated slang for being in the know, well informed
a tic is an involuntary muscle spasm

explanation.surface: A knowledgeable person discussing a muscle spasm caused by the liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is just a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepatic means relating to or affecting the liver, a medical adjective.

clue.text: I take a small magazine to first 20th century poet?

parts.note: mag is a short form of magazine
first is written 1ST, and the digit 1 looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: Someone taking a little magazine to the earliest modern poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Imagists were an early twentieth-century school of poets such as Pound, so one of them is such a poet.

clue.text: Enclose, in Sri Lanka, a snake

parts.note: CL is the international vehicle code for Sri Lanka, from its old name Ceylon
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Trapping a snake found in Sri Lanka.
explanation.definitionFit: To inclasp is to clasp in or hold around, so to enclose.

clue.text: Puppet under complete control

parts.note: a marionette is worked by cords from above, so anyone wholly controlled by another is described with the same image

explanation.surface: A marionette entirely in the hands of its operator.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone manipulated by another, like a dangling marionette.

clue.text: Marsupial, by the way, is in the hen house!

parts.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a marsupial
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo has found its way into the chicken coop.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the place where hens perch to sleep, a henhouse.

clue.text: Corpulent man is calamitous

parts.note: corpulent means fat
Al is a man's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: An overweight man is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatal means causing death or disaster, close to disastrous.

clue.text: Ray of light bouncing off marble sea

indicators.note: letters bouncing off each other are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Sunlight reflecting off a sea that looks like marble.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a narrow, intense ray of light.

clue.text: Genuine gold then titanium and carbon as well

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
taken as written
Ti is the chemical symbol for titanium
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A real alloy containing gold, titanium and carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real, not fake.

clue.text: Carry away a vehicle, for instance

explanation.surface: Taking off a car as an example of something that carries.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport is to convey or enrapture someone, and a vehicle is one means of conveying people.

clue.text: Solomon's mother, beth, has a ba surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A biblical note about Solomon's mother, mixing Hebrew letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The lone 'a' between 'has' and 'ba' is a link; the fodder is BETH, HAS and BA, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Bathsheba, wife of David, bore King Solomon.

clue.text: Dog crying out to live here

explanation.surface: A barking dog suggests a place to settle.
explanation.walkthrough: BARKING is a district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's loud cry is a bark, and Barking is a town in east London where people live.

clue.text: Fabric that's very loud in a Tate sort of way

indicators.note: in places the musical marking inside the rearranged letters
a sort of thing is a version of it, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A loud fabric that suits the style of the Tate gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A TATE as TAETA, and 'in' puts FF inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven fabric, often silk.

clue.text: Show the original television to everyone

indicators.note: the original letter is the first one of the word that follows

parts.note: each means every one

explanation.surface: Showing the first ever television broadcast to all viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: To teach is to instruct or demonstrate, as when you show someone how.

clue.text: Memory loss of men drunk on the continent

indicators.note: on here sets the scrambled word within the continent

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: drunk suggests something reeling and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Drinkers abroad who cannot remember what happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns MEN into MNE, which 'on' places inside ASIA after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for losing one's memory.

clue.text: Hold a proportion for this admiral

parts.note: ho is an old cry meaning stop or hold
a ratio is a proportion between quantities

explanation.surface: Keeping things in proportion for a naval officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Nelson was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio was Nelson's first name, so he is the admiral meant.

clue.text: Whether to the left or right, the umpire displays hesitation

annotationWithheld.why: Whether to the left or right, the umpire displays hesitation (5): REF + ER read both ways, but no clue word defines REFER
annotationWithheld.clue: Whether to the left or right, the umpire displays hesitation

clue.text: Fluttering terns were resident in the occident

indicators.note: fluttering suggests birds flapping about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Seabirds flapping about over someone living in the west.
explanation.definitionFit: The occident is the west, so a person living there is from the western world.

clue.text: Bet the composer misplaced a note

indicators.note: misplaced means lost, so a letter goes missing from the composer

parts.note: Richard Wagner was the German composer of the Ring cycle
n is the dictionary abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: Wagering that the composer lost a page of his score.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a stake placed on an uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Islamic ruler found in supreme ergonomic environment

indicators.note: found in says the letters are sitting inside the following words

explanation.surface: A ruler discovered in an office of ideal design.
explanation.definitionFit: An emeer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler or commander.

clue.text: Huge mass of frozen lettuce!

explanation.surface: Lettuce left in the freezer as a solid block.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a floating mass of ice, and also a crisp variety of lettuce.

clue.text: Series of deliveries to court session caused disorder

parts.note: an over is a series of six balls bowled in cricket
a set is a unit of play in tennis, on court

explanation.surface: A cricket over and a tennis set together caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overset is an old verb for upset or overturn, so disturbed or threw into confusion.

clue.text: Lightweight damage to a school

parts.note: a gram is a small unit of weight
mar means damage

explanation.surface: A minor bit of damage done to a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A GRAMMAR school is a selective British state secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar is short for grammar school, a type of British secondary school.

clue.text: Ripped through a party like the wind

parts.note: ripped means torn
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Something tore through a party like a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm.
